page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-32 is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Network Optimized family, designed for high memory density. It is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 496.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core allocation of 15.5 GB per virtual CPU. The instance does not include integrated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs.

The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disk volumes for all file system and persistent data needs. Additionally, it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external IP reservations or network routing gateways for public internet reachability. Hardware features such as hardware-assisted virtualization or AVX extensions are not reported as exposed in this profile configuration.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency standpoint, the server is configured to deliver high RAM density per compute unit. This design prioritizes memory-bound throughput over raw CPU parallelism, eliminating the overhead of paying for unneeded CPU cycles or dedicated local NVMe drives when workloads require substantial memory capacities. Consequently, the m4n-hypermem-32 is suited for large in-memory databases, memory-resident analytics, caching layers, and high-footprint enterprise applications.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-32 is a high-memory server instance within the Network Optimized series, running on dedicated 64-bit x86 architecture. The configuration features 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 496.0 GB of RAM, yielding an expansive ratio of 15.5 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no integrated GPUs and provides no local physical storage, requiring attached network storage volumes for file systems and data persistence. Furthermore, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Economically and architecturally, m4n-hypermem-32 is structured for systems that require extensive RAM capacity without incurring the resource costs of excessive CPU compute. This architecture makes the instance suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caches, real-time analytics engines, and memory-intensive enterprise business workloads.
